title: A Sketchbook at the Park
description: Draw a park view on the pages of a portable art book.
cardDescription: Draw a park view on the pages of a portable art book.
focus: The setting is a Sketchbook at the Park. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Writing tool with a graphite core
One side of a sheet in a book
Make a picture with a pencil
Tall plant with a woody trunk
Material used for writing or wrapping
Creative work such as drawing or painting
Line around the outside of a shape
One movement of a brush or pencil

answerNotes.PENCIL: The writing core of a modern pencil is graphite, not metallic lead. Lead remains a traditional everyday name for it.
answerNotes.PAGE: A page is one side of a book's paper. A single physical leaf normally has two pages, front and back.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.ERASER: An eraser removes many graphite marks by rubbing them from the paper. It does not work the same way on every kind of ink.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Straight mark drawn with a ruler
Long pole used with a fishing reel
Spool storing film or fishing line
Food used to attract a fish
Rest on top of water rather than sink
Weight used to take a fishing line down
Water animal with fins and gills
Container with a base and sides
Open mesh used to catch fish
Throw a fishing line out over the water

answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
answerNotes.REEL: A reel stores a long flexible strip or line. A fishing reel takes up line, while a film reel holds a strip of images.
answerNotes.FISH: Fish live in water and breathe through gills. A seal or otter swims too, but it is a mammal rather than a fish.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.BANK: In a water scene, bank means the ground beside a river or creek. In a money scene, it names a financial business.

words: Two-lens viewing tool for watching distant birds
Animal with feathers and a beak
Carrying band attached to a bag
Part a bird spreads to fly
Book that helps identify birds or places
What someone sees through a window

answerNotes.BIRD: Birds have feathers, beaks, and wings. Not every bird flies, so feathers are a more dependable identifying feature than flight alone.
answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.
answerNotes.FEATHER: Feathers help birds with warmth and, in many species, flight. Small soft down feathers have a different job from long wing feathers.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note is a short written message. It can be a reminder, a greeting, or a brief explanation attached to an object.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Transparent piece that sharpens an image
Camera mechanism that opens to admit light for an exposure
Small control pressed to take a photograph
Strip used to secure or carry something
Container fitted around a small item
Image made with a camera or pencil
Sharp cracking sound when something breaks

answerNotes.CAMERA: A camera records pictures. Its lens focuses the scene, while a shutter or electronic control determines when light is recorded.
answerNotes.PHOTO: Photo is short for photograph. A caption or name label can preserve information that the image alone does not supply.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button fastens through a buttonhole or loop. Some have holes through the face; others attach by a small shank on the back.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.

words: Light framed toy flown at the end of a line
Rear extension of an animal's body

Hue, such as red or blue
Four-sided outline of a familiar kite shape

answerNotes.STRING: String is a thin cord used for tying or flying a kite. A kite's string connects the flying frame to the person holding it.
answerNotes.TAIL: Tail can name the rear part of an animal or a trailing end of ribbon or a kite. The word describes different things with a similar extending position.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
answerNotes.REEL: A reel stores a long flexible strip or line. A fishing reel takes up line, while a film reel holds a strip of images.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
